subject.title: [Feature]: Skill author-defined setup hook (run skill-supplied script on install/update)

question: Should OpenClaw core own automatic skill-authored setup execution during install/update, or should setup remain an explicit ClawHub/plugin-admin workflow backed by stable installed-skill SDK helpers?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses a host-execution and skill trust boundary; source inspection confirms the capability is missing, but automation cannot choose the product/security contract or default consent model safely.

options.title: Approve a guarded core lifecycle hook
options.body: Define an explicit opt-in metadata contract, install/update consent behavior, env/path allowlist rules, docs, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep setup as explicit plugin/admin RPC
options.body: Close the automatic lifecycle direction and support the existing ClawHub plugin pattern plus stable SDK helpers for operators who intentionally run setup.

options.title: Defer until installed-skill SDK lands
options.body: Keep this issue blocked on #81913/#81921 so the plugin surface can mature before choosing whether core lifecycle execution is needed.

recommendation.title: Approve a guarded core lifecycle hook
recommendation.body: Define an explicit opt-in metadata contract, install/update consent behavior, env/path allowlist rules, docs, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the broadest product/security boundary choice across ClawHub, skill install UX, and core host execution policy among the identified area owners.
